definition: Yehoshua Bar-Hillel (Hebrew: יהושע בר-הלל; 8 September 1915 – 25 September 1975) was an Israeli philosopher, mathematician, and linguist.
details: He was a pioneer in the fields of machine translation and formal linguistics.
story: Picture a translator at the United Nations, listening to one language and whispering the meaning into another in real time. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. Meaning lives in company — a word is known by the words it keeps. That pattern-earned fluency is Yehoshua Bar-Hillel.
